chunks: My father narrated to him, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Yaqoob ibn Yazid, from Marwan ibn Ubayd, from the one he mentioned, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He said: For high-quality goods there are two prayers, and for bad goods there are two prayers. It is said to the owner of the high-quality good: 'May God bless you and the one who sold it to you.' And it is said to the owner of the bad good: 'May God not bless you and the one who sold it to you.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic etiquette for praying or cursing regarding good and bad quality goods in trade?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith to illustrate the Prophetic tradition of 'du'a' (prayer) and 'la'na' (curse) as social markers of quality in commercial transactions. The Imam specifies that for high-quality goods (al-Jayyid), one prays for both the seller and the buyer, whereas for defective goods (al-Raddi'), one curses both, emphasizing shared responsibility in the exchange's value. This practice underscores the ethical dimension of trade in Shia jurisprudence, where satisfaction and quality dictate the spiritual tone of the transaction.
